title: Affine line-section neighbourhoods on a regular separated scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact regular scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Assume $X$ is separated: its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ has closed-immersion diagonal [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every point $x\in X$ there exist an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and a global section $t\in\Gamma(X,A)$ such that $x\in X_t$ and $X_t$ is affine. Here $X_t$ is the nonvanishing locus of $t$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The module $A$ may depend on $x$; no single ample invertible module on $X$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GML, lemma-regular-ample-family, specialized to a separated scheme (a closed-immersion diagonal is affine). Morphisms Definition 0FXR, definition-family-ample-invertible-modules: absorb its positive exponent into the chosen invertible module.

proof.text: By [def-weil-regular-scheme], $X$ is locally Noetherian; together with its quasi-compactness this makes it Noetherian. Clauses (1) and (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] give finitely many pairwise disjoint open and closed normal integral components covering $X$. Fix $x$ and let $Y$ be its component, $Z=X\setminus Y$. The closed subset $Y$ is quasi-compact: add $Z$ to any open cover of $Y$ and use quasi-compactness of $X$. It is locally Noetherian by restriction to the open $Y$ [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Its stalks are the same regular local rings as those of $X$, so $Y$ is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Finally $\Delta_Y$ is the base change of $\Delta_X$ along $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Y\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$; hence it is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Thus $Y$ is integral, Noetherian, regular and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tags 0569 (lemma-regular-normal) and 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian), as used in Divisors Tag 0GML (lemma-regular-ample-family), first two sentences; Morphisms Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $x\in U\subseteq Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Since $Y$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], it is irreducible, and $U$ is nonempty. If $U$ were not dense, the complement of its closure would be a nonempty open disjoint from $U$, contradicting irreducibility. Put $E=|Y|\setminus|U|$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], $E=E_1\cup\cdots\cup E_r$ for its finitely many irreducible components. Give each $E_i$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. This is a nonempty reduced irreducible scheme, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Each $E_i$ has a generic point $\xi_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. If $E=\varnothing$, take $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GML (lemma-regular-ample-family), choose an affine neighbourhood; Tag 0BCW (lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor), finite irreducible boundary components; Properties Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-affine-open-boundary-codimension-one] to $Y$ and $U$. The ambient scheme is separated and locally Noetherian by step 1, and the open is affine and dense by step 2. It gives $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,\xi_i}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $y\in Y$ and $\mathcal I_i$ the ideal sheaf of $E_i$. If $y
otin E_i$, then $(\mathcal I_i)_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, generated by the nonzerodivisor $1$. If $y\in E_i$, choose an affine open $y\in V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. As a nonempty open of the irreducible $E_i$, $E_i\cap V$ is irreducible and contains $\xi_i$, so it is $V(\mathfrak q)$ for the prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$ of $\xi_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] (1), $\mathcal I_i(V)$ is the radical ideal with zero set $V(\mathfrak q)$, that is $\mathfrak q$, and $\mathcal I_i|_V=\widetilde{\mathfrak q}$. Let $\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak q$ be the prime of $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (c), $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi_i}=R_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] $(\mathcal I_i)_y=\mathfrak qA$, a prime ideal of $A$. The primes of $A$ contained in $\mathfrak qA$ correspond to the primes of $R$ contained in $\mathfrak q$, hence to the primes of $R_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $\dim R_{\mathfrak q}=1$, the prime $\mathfrak qA$ is nonzero and no prime lies strictly between $0$ and $\mathfrak qA$: it has height one. By step 1 and [def-weil-regular-scheme], $A$ is a regular local ring, so [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] with $r=0$ makes $A$ a Noetherian unique factorization domain. By [lem-trf-ufd-height-one], (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii), $\mathfrak qA=(f_i)$ for some $f_i\in A$. As $\mathfrak qA
e0$, $f_i
e0$, and multiplication by $f_i$ is injective in the domain $A$. So every stalk $(\mathcal I_i)_y$ has a nonzerodivisor generator $f_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BCW (lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor), using Tag 0BCV (lemma-complement-affine-open) and the proof of Tag 0AGA (lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD); local factoriality from More on Algebra Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD) as in Tag 0GML, and Algebra Tag 0AFT (lemma-characterize-UFD-height-1).

proof.text: Repeatedly apply [lem-weil-pbc-product-ideal-closed-subscheme-union] to construct a closed subscheme $D\hookrightarrow Y$ with ideal $\mathcal I=\prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal I_i$ and support $|D|=\bigcup_iE_i=E$. For $r=0$ take the empty closed subscheme with unit ideal. We verify the Cartier condition on stalks. At $y\in Y$ each $(\mathcal I_i)_y=(f_i)$ has a nonzerodivisor generator by step 3. Products of ideal sheaves are the affine-local products in [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Passing to the stalk gives $\mathcal I_y=\prod_i(\mathcal I_i)_y$: in a localization a finite sum of products of fractions can be put over a common denominator, and conversely every fraction whose numerator is in a product ideal is a sum of products of fractions from the factors. Thus $\mathcal I_y=(\prod_i f_i)$. Multiplication by this product is injective, by cancelling the nonzerodivisors successively; for $r=0$ the generator is $1$. The scheme form of [lem-sfb-stalk-nonzerodivisor-cartier-spreading] applies to the closed subscheme $D$ in the locally Noetherian scheme $Y$ and proves that $\mathcal I$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Hence $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor, with $Y\setminus|D|=U$.

source.place: Tag 0BCW (lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor), final sum of the boundary divisors; Tag 0AG8 (lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points), clause (2), for the explicitly verified stalk condition.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-invertible], $L=\mathcal I^\vee=\mathcal O_Y(D)$ is invertible. By [lem-sc-canonical-section-zero-scheme] its canonical section $s=1_D$ has zero scheme exactly $D$. To relate this to the nonvanishing locus of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], choose a local frame of $L$ and write $s=a$ in this frame. The image ideal defining its zero scheme [def-pc-zero-scheme] is then $(a)$, so a point belongs to $|D|$ exactly when $a$ maps to zero in its residue field, equivalently when its germ lies in the maximal ideal. Therefore $Y_s=Y\setminus|D|=U$, an affine open containing $x$.

source.place: Tag 0GML (lemma-regular-ample-family), canonical-section conclusion; Tag 01WX (definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor), clause (2); Tag 01X0 (lemma-characterize-OD); Tag 02OQ (definition-zero-scheme-s).

proof.text: Extend the module and section from the open and closed component $Y$ to $X=Y\amalg Z$ explicitly. For every open $V\subseteq X$ set $A(V)=L(V\cap Y)\times\mathcal O_Z(V\cap Z)$ with componentwise restrictions and $\mathcal O_X(V)$-action through its restrictions. This is a module sheaf since compatible local sections glue uniquely in each factor. Its restrictions are $L$ on $Y$ and $\mathcal O_Z$ on $Z$; their local frames form an open cover of $X$ by frames of $A$, so $A$ is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Take $t=(s,0)\in\Gamma(X,A)$. By the stalk definition of nonvanishing in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], it is nonvanishing precisely at the points of $Y_s$ and nowhere on $Z$. Thus $X_t=U$ is affine and contains $x$, as required. The empty $X$ has no points to check.
